goldenPoints: Therapeutic index = TD50/ED50: the wider it is, the safer the drug
Prazosin causes first-dose postural hypotension; tamsulosin is the uroselective answer in BPH
Methanol poisoning is treated with fomepizole; iron poisoning with desferrioxamine
Ethambutol damages the optic nerve — red-green colour vision goes first
Bedaquiline kills TB bacilli by blocking their ATP synthase
Warfarin in pregnancy is teratogenic — heparin/LMWH is the anticoagulant of pregnancy
Cisplatin's dose-limiter is nephrotoxicity (plus ototoxicity); carboplatin's is myelosuppression
Bleomycin scars the lungs and spares the marrow — pulmonary fibrosis is its signature
SGLT2 inhibitors cause glucosuria and genital candidiasis; metformin risks lactic acidosis
MAO inhibitors plus tyramine in wine/cheese = hypertensive crisis
intro: Pharmacology carries 13 questions per FMGE paper, and the previous-year stems follow a strict formula: mechanism of action, drug of choice, classic adverse effect, antidote. Almost nothing is asked about doses. Learn every drug here as a four-part card — class, mechanism, one signature use, one signature toxicity — and most stems become one-liners.

branches.label: CVS & Diuretics
leaves: HF mortality: BB, ACEi, MRA, ARNI

subject: Pharmacology
tagline: FMGE asks mechanism, drug of choice, signature side effect and antidote — rarely anything else

topics.askedAs: therapeutic index, inhibition graphs, bioavailability meaning
topics.oneLiner: Competitive shifts the curve right; non-competitive pulls it down — and a wide therapeutic index means a forgiving drug.
points: Pharmacodynamics = what the drug does to the body; pharmacokinetics = what the body does to the drug
Therapeutic index = TD50 ÷ ED50; higher value = safer drug (penicillin wide, lithium/digoxin narrow)
Competitive inhibition: Km increases, Vmax unchanged — overcome by more substrate
Non-competitive inhibition: Vmax falls, Km unchanged
Bioavailability 30% means only 30% reaches systemic circulation unchanged — first-pass metabolism is the usual reason
Drugs NOT metabolised by acetylation are the exceptions to remember: most others (INH, sulfonamides, hydralazine, procainamide) are
Slow acetylators develop INH-induced peripheral neuritis more easily — prevented by pyridoxine
Zero-order kinetics: constant amount cleared per unit time (alcohol, phenytoin at high levels)
Prodrugs need activation: levodopa, enalapril, clopidogrel, codeine
topics.title: General Pharmacology: Kinetics & Dynamics
topics.trap: Therapeutic index uses TD50 (toxic dose), not LD50, in the standard pharmacology definition tested here.

topics.askedAs: poisoning vignette, myasthenia drug of choice, botulinum mechanism
topics.oneLiner: Too much ACh → atropine plus pralidoxime; too little at the junction → pyridostigmine.
points: Organophosphate poisoning: SLUDGE signs, miosis, bradycardia, low plasma cholinesterase — atropine blocks muscarinic effects
Pralidoxime reactivates cholinesterase but only before ageing of the enzyme occurs
Atropine does NOT reverse muscle paralysis in OP poisoning — that needs the oxime
Myasthenia gravis drug of choice: pyridostigmine (neostigmine family); edrophonium is the diagnostic test drug
Botulinum toxin blocks acetylcholine RELEASE from nerve terminals — flaccid paralysis results
Succinylcholine triggers malignant hyperthermia in susceptible patients — treated with dantrolene
Atracurium is eliminated by Hofmann elimination — ideal in renal/hepatic failure
Physostigmine crosses the blood-brain barrier (tertiary amine); neostigmine does not
topics.title: ANS: Cholinergic & Neuromuscular Drugs
topics.trap: Pilocarpine-like pictures with pinpoint pupils and respiratory distress in a child = cholinergic poisoning, not opioid — pupils mislead; check salivation and secretions.

topics.askedAs: alpha-blocker choice in BPH, pheochromocytoma preparation
topics.oneLiner: Phenoxybenzamine before surgery for pheo; tamsulosin for the prostate; prazosin drops the first-dose patient.
points: Prazosin (alpha-1 blocker) causes first-dose postural hypotension — dizziness on standing
Tamsulosin is uroselective (alpha-1A) — preferred alpha-blocker in BPH, least hypotension
Phenoxybenzamine (irreversible alpha blocker) is the preoperative drug for pheochromocytoma — alpha blockade BEFORE any beta blockade
Labetalol blocks both alpha and beta receptors — used in hypertensive emergencies and pregnancy
Beta-blocker uses: hypertension, angina, post-MI, heart failure, thyrotoxicosis, migraine prophylaxis, glaucoma
Beta-blockers are relatively contraindicated in asthma/COPD and decompensated heart block — diabetes alone is NOT a contraindication
COMT inhibitors (entacapone) prolong levodopa action in Parkinson disease
Clonidine withdrawal causes rebound hypertension
topics.title: Adrenergic Drugs & Blockers
topics.trap: Beta blockade before alpha blockade in pheochromocytoma leaves alpha vasoconstriction unopposed — hypertensive crisis.

topics.askedAs: mortality-reducing drug, pregnancy-safe vs banned antihypertensives
topics.oneLiner: In pregnancy: methyldopa and labetalol yes, ACE inhibitors never.
points: Drugs proven to reduce mortality in heart failure: beta-blockers, ACE inhibitors/ARNI, aldosterone antagonists, SGLT2 inhibitors
Methyldopa and labetalol are safe in pregnancy hypertension; hydralazine is also used
ACE inhibitors and ARBs are contraindicated in pregnancy (fetal renal damage) and in bilateral renal artery stenosis
A pregnant woman with DVT gets heparin/LMWH — warfarin is teratogenic
Statins lower LDL most powerfully; fibrates (PPAR-alpha agonists like fenofibrate) lower triglycerides best
Orlistat's commonest adverse effect is oily stools/steatorrhoea (pancreatic lipase inhibitor)
Hypertensive emergency with encephalopathy: IV labetalol or nicardipine are standard choices
Thiazide-induced hypokalaemia is prevented by adding a potassium-sparing drug (spironolactone/amiloride)
topics.title: CVS Drugs, Diuretics & Lipid Agents
topics.trap: ACE inhibitor + NSAID + diuretic is the 'triple whammy' for acute kidney injury — a favourite interaction stem.

topics.askedAs: warfarin target, pregnancy anticoagulant, rivaroxaban mechanism
topics.oneLiner: Mechanical valve on warfarin: INR 2.5-3.5; pregnant patient: heparin, always.
points: Warfarin (like dicumarol) blocks vitamin K epoxide reductase — factors II, VII, IX, X and proteins C/S fall
Target INR for mechanical heart valves: 2.5-3.5 (higher than the 2-3 for most other indications)
Heparin potentiates antithrombin III; protamine reverses unfractionated heparin
Rivaroxaban and apixaban directly inhibit factor Xa
Alteplase (tPA) converts plasminogen to plasmin — fibrinolytic of choice in acute ischaemic stroke/MI
Aspirin irreversibly acetylates platelet COX for the platelet's whole life (~7-10 days)
Clopidogrel blocks the platelet P2Y12 ADP receptor and needs CYP activation
Vitamin K is the specific antidote for warfarin over-anticoagulation (with PCC/FFP when bleeding)
topics.title: Anticoagulants, Antiplatelets & Fibrinolytics
topics.trap: Warfarin's earliest casualty is protein C — hence warfarin-induced skin necrosis in protein C deficiency.

topics.oneLiner: Doxycycline blocks the 30S, macrolides the 50S, quinolones the gyrase — mechanisms are pure profit.
points: Doxycycline inhibits bacterial protein synthesis at the 30S ribosomal subunit
Fluoroquinolones inhibit DNA gyrase/topoisomerase — signature harms: tendinitis and Achilles tendon rupture
Metronidazole + alcohol → disulfiram-like reaction (flushing, nausea, hypotension)
Penicillin allergy plus need for cover: macrolides are the usual substitute class tested
Aminoglycosides are ototoxic and nephrotoxic; they need oxygen-dependent uptake (useless against anaerobes)
Vancomycin infusion too fast → red man syndrome (histamine release, not true allergy)
Linezolid is a weak MAO inhibitor — serotonin syndrome risk with SSRIs
Beta-lactamase inhibitors (clavulanate) rescue penicillins from bacterial enzymes
Chloramphenicol: aplastic anaemia and grey baby syndrome
topics.title: Antimicrobials: Mechanisms & Signature Harms
topics.trap: Achilles tendonitis after an antibiotic = fluoroquinolone until proven otherwise.

topics.askedAs: ATT adverse-effect map, resistance definitions, katG
topics.oneLiner: Ethambutol blinds, INH resistance is katG, bedaquiline starves the bacillus of ATP.
points: Ethambutol causes optic neuritis — red-green colour vision is lost first
Isoniazid resistance maps to mutations in the katG gene (catalase-peroxidase)
Bedaquiline inhibits mycobacterial ATP synthase — the energy factory is its target
XDR-TB: resistance to INH + rifampicin PLUS a fluoroquinolone PLUS an injectable/second-line agent
Rifampicin is a potent enzyme inducer — it lowers levels of warfarin, OCPs and many ART drugs
Rifampicin turns urine and tears orange — warn the patient, it is harmless
Streptomycin and other injectable ATT drugs are avoided in pregnancy (fetal ototoxicity)
Leprosy reactions and drug adverse effects are asked as pairs — dapsone causes haemolysis in G6PD deficiency
topics.title: Anti-TB & Anti-Leprosy Drugs
topics.trap: On ART plus ATT, rifampicin's enzyme induction — not toxicity — is the usual reason doses must change.

topics.askedAs: drug-of-choice and avoid-in scenarios for diabetes
topics.oneLiner: Desmopressin for central DI, metformin fears acid, gliptin linagliptin spares the kidney dose maths.
points: Metformin is linked to lactic acidosis (the biguanide legacy of phenformin) — risk rises in renal failure
SGLT2 inhibitors (dapagliflozin class) cause glucosuria — and genital/vulval candidiasis; avoid when candida is the problem
Sulfonylureas are the classic oral drugs causing hypoglycaemia during exercise/fasting
Linagliptin needs NO dose adjustment in chronic kidney disease (biliary excretion)
Desmopressin (DDAVP) is the drug of choice for central diabetes insipidus
Fibrates act through PPAR-alpha; statins inhibit HMG-CoA reductase
Pegvisomant blocks the growth hormone receptor in acromegaly; octreotide suppresses GH release
Tamoxifen is a SERM — antagonist in breast, agonist in endometrium (endometrial cancer risk) and bone
topics.title: Endocrine & Antidiabetic Drugs
topics.trap: Glucosuria after starting a diabetes drug is the SGLT2 inhibitor working — not worsening diabetes.

topics.askedAs: antidepressant selection by side-effect profile, lithium facts
topics.oneLiner: Cheese + MAOI = crisis; bupropion spares the bedroom; phenytoin grows the gums.
points: Phenytoin: gum hypertrophy, hirsutism, osteomalacia, teratogenicity (fetal hydantoin syndrome)
Lamotrigine's feared adverse effect: Stevens-Johnson syndrome — stop for any rash
Ethosuximide blocks T-type calcium channels — drug for absence seizures
MAO inhibitors + tyramine (wine, cheese) → hypertensive crisis
Bupropion is the antidepressant chosen when sexual dysfunction must be avoided (also helps smoking cessation, like varenicline)
SSRIs block serotonin reuptake only; SNRIs (venlafaxine) block serotonin AND noradrenaline
Lithium: narrow therapeutic index, tremor, hypothyroidism, nephrogenic DI; toxicity worsened by thiazides and dehydration
Metoclopramide (antiemetic) causes acute dystonia and other extrapyramidal effects via D2 blockade
Status epilepticus first-line: benzodiazepine (lorazepam/diazepam), then levetiracetam or phenytoin
topics.title: CNS Drugs: Epilepsy, Depression, Psychosis
topics.trap: Acute dystonia after an antiemetic or antipsychotic is drug-induced — treat with an anticholinergic (promethazine/benztropine), not more dopamine blockade.

topics.askedAs: cisplatin vs carboplatin, bleomycin lung, targeted therapy matches
topics.oneLiner: Cisplatin kills kidneys and hearing; carboplatin kills marrow; bleomycin kills lungs.
points: Cisplatin: highly emetogenic, nephrotoxic and ototoxic — hydration is mandatory
Carboplatin differs by causing MORE myelosuppression and less nephro/ototoxicity
Bleomycin causes pulmonary fibrosis, worsened by high oxygen and radiation — and barely touches the marrow
Methotrexate inhibits dihydrofolate reductase; leucovorin (folinic acid) rescues normal cells
5-Fluorouracil starves DNA synthesis by blocking thymidylate synthase; hand-foot syndrome is its skin signature
Imatinib (BCR-ABL/KIT tyrosine kinase inhibitor) treats both CML and GIST
Trastuzumab targets HER2 in breast cancer — cardiotoxicity is its watch-point
Filgrastim (G-CSF) is the drug for chemotherapy-induced neutropenia
Ondansetron (5-HT3 blocker) anchors chemotherapy antiemetic prophylaxis, with dexamethasone and NK1 blockers
topics.title: Anticancer Drugs & Targeted Therapy
topics.trap: Radiation recalls and worsens bleomycin lung injury — the lung, not the marrow, is bleomycin's victim.

topics.askedAs: antidote matched to the poison in the vignette
points: Methanol poisoning (hooch tragedy): fomepizole (or ethanol) blocks alcohol dehydrogenase; vision is at stake
Iron tablet overdose in a child: desferrioxamine is the chelator-antidote
Benzodiazepine overdose: flumazenil — used cautiously (seizure risk in dependent patients)
Opioid poisoning (pinpoint pupils, respiratory depression): naloxone
Malignant hyperthermia after succinylcholine/halothane: dantrolene releases the calcium brake in muscle
Acute mountain sickness: acetazolamide is the drug of choice for prevention and treatment
Pheochromocytoma patients get phenoxybenzamine preoperatively to blunt catecholamine surges
Paracetamol overdose: N-acetylcysteine replenishes glutathione
Carbon monoxide poisoning: 100% oxygen — carboxyhaemoglobin has a cherry-red colour
topics.title: Toxicology: Poisonings & Antidotes
topics.trap: Flumazenil can precipitate seizures in chronic benzodiazepine users — the antidote itself has a trap built in.

topics.askedAs: fixed drug eruption, altitude, H. pylori regimen class logic
topics.oneLiner: Same spot, same drug, every time = fixed drug eruption — classically NSAIDs and sulfonamides.
points: Fixed drug eruption: rash recurs at the EXACT same site on re-exposure — NSAIDs and sulfonamides are classic culprits
H. pylori eradication = PPI plus two antibiotics (clarithromycin + amoxicillin/metronidazole classes)
PPIs irreversibly block the gastric H+/K+ ATPase — the final common pathway of acid secretion
Zileuton inhibits 5-lipoxygenase (leukotriene synthesis); montelukast blocks the leukotriene receptor
Omalizumab (anti-IgE) is the monoclonal added in severe allergic asthma — not a bronchodilator
Roflumilast (PDE4 inhibitor) is the add-on tested in severe COPD on top of LABA therapy
Non-sedating antihistamines (fexofenadine, loratadine) are preferred over cetirizine when drowsiness is the complaint
Allopurinol (xanthine oxidase inhibitor, a purine analogue) is the chronic gout drug; colchicine treats the acute attack
Rasburicase/allopurinol prevent tumour lysis uric acid injury — rasburicase acts fastest by breaking uric acid down
topics.title: Autacoids, GI, Respiratory & Miscellaneous
topics.trap: Omalizumab is never an acute asthma drug — nothing that works over weeks rescues an attack tonight.
